purpose: Bisacodyl is used to treat constipation and help you have a bowel movement. It is also used to clean out your bowel before certain medical procedures like a colonoscopy. It gives you relief usually within 6 to 12 hours when taken by mouth, or within 15 to 60 minutes when used as a suppository.
how_it_works: Bisacodyl works by directly stimulating the muscles in your intestines, causing them to squeeze and push stool through more quickly. It also helps draw water into the bowel, which softens the stool and makes it easier to pass. Think of it as giving your intestines a gentle nudge to get things moving.
common_side_effects: You may notice stomach cramps or discomfort, nausea, diarrhea, or a feeling of urgency to use the bathroom. Some people feel bloated or gassy. These effects are usually mild and go away after your bowel movement.
warnings: Do not use bisacodyl for more than 7 days in a row unless your doctor tells you to, as overuse can make your bowel dependent on laxatives. Avoid taking it within one hour of drinking milk or taking antacids, as this can cause stomach irritation. Do not use it if you have stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting, as these could be signs of a more serious problem. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have any bowel disease.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 and older, the usual dose is 1 to 3 tablets (5 mg each) taken by mouth at bedtime, or one 10 mg suppository inserted rectally. Children under 12 should only use this medicine under a doctor's guidance. Swallow tablets whole — do not chew or crush them.
